pattern: \$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
plain: You used $ on a vector, but $ only works on lists and data frames.
causes: The variable holds an atomic vector (numeric, character, logical) rather than a data.frame or list.
A function returned a vector or single column instead of a data frame.
A column selection with [ ] simplified to a vector (use drop = FALSE).
fix: Check class(x) to inspect the object. If x is a data frame, verify it was not reduced to a vector.

plain: R looked for a name and found nothing bound to it.
causes: The name is misspelled, or the capitalisation differs: R is case sensitive.
It was created in an earlier session and is not in this one.
It exists, but not where this code can see it: inside a function only arguments and outer scopes are visible.
fix: Check the spelling, run the code that creates it, or print ls() to see what does exist.

plain: R does not know a function by that name.
causes: The package it lives in is installed but not attached: no library() call has run.
A typo, or a name from another language (len() is Python; R uses length()).
A variable with the same name is shadowing the function.
fix: Add library(packageName) near the top, or type the name in the console without brackets to see what R has bound to it.

pattern: argument "([^"]+)" is missing, with no default
plain: A function was called without an argument it needs.
causes: The argument was left out.
The argument name is misspelled, so R sees one unnamed argument and one missing.
fix: Check the signature with ?function_name: every argument without a default must be supplied.

plain: An argument was passed that this function does not accept.
causes: The name is misspelled, or it belongs to a different function.
The function changed and no longer takes that argument.
fix: Compare the call with ?function_name -- argument names must match exactly.

plain: R expected numbers and got text.
causes: A column was read as text (read.csv() keeps anything that does not look numeric as text).
A number arrived as a string: "5" is not 5.
as.numeric() was applied to a factor and returned level numbers instead of values.
fix: Check the type with class(x) or str(x), then convert deliberately: as.numeric(as.character(x)).

plain: Something was indexed at a position that does not exist.
causes: The index is past the end of the vector or data frame.
An empty result was indexed: x[1] where x has length 0.
The data has fewer rows than the number in the code assumes.
fix: Print length(x) or nrow(df) first, and prefer seq_len(nrow(df)) to a fixed range.

plain: A column was assigned a vector of the wrong length.
causes: The replacement is longer or shorter than the number of rows.
One side was filtered and the other was not.
fix: Build the replacement from the same object, e.g. df$new <- df$existing * 2.

pattern: object of type 'closure' is not subsettable
plain: A function was used where data was expected.
causes: A variable shares a name with a function this code calls (df, c, t and data are the usual culprits).
A function's name was used as if it held the function's result.
fix: Rename the variable, or refer to the result of the call rather than the function itself.

plain: if() was given a vector of TRUE/FALSE values but needs exactly one.
causes: The condition compares a whole column rather than a single value.
A filter or loop was intended, not a branch.
fix: Use any(condition), all(condition), or the vectorised ifelse()/filter instead.

plain: A condition evaluated to NA, so R could not decide which way to go.
causes: A comparison involved NA: x == NA is NA, always.
A column has missing values that were never handled.
fix: Test with is.na(x) and decide explicitly what missing values should do.

plain: R could not finish reading this code: it is a syntax problem, not a runtime one.
causes: A bracket or quote is not closed on this line, or on an earlier one.
A comma is missing or extra inside a call.
Lines were run separately that R needs to see together.
fix: Look at the line R quotes and one line above it: brackets pair up, and the error often points just past the real cause.

plain: R could not read or write the file you named.
causes: The path is relative and the working directory is not what you expect: getwd() shows it.
The file's name or case differs from what is on disk.
The folder does not exist yet.
fix: Print getwd() and list.files(), then use the Files pane to set the directory.

plain: The package is not installed.
causes: It was never installed on this machine.
It is installed for a different R version or library path.
fix: Install it once with install.packages("name"), then library(name).

pattern: number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length
plain: You are trying to replace part of an object, but the sizes don't line up.
causes: Assigning 3 values into a space that expects 5.
Trying to replace a subset of a vector with a vector of a different length.
fix: Check the length of the items you are replacing and the length of the new values. They must match, or the new values must be a perfect multiple.

pattern: arguments imply differing number of rows
plain: You are trying to create a data frame, but the columns are of different lengths.
causes: Combining vectors of length 5 and length 6 into a `data.frame()`.
Creating a tibble with variables that do not have matching row counts.
fix: Check the `length()` of each vector you are trying to combine and make sure they are exactly the same.

pattern: cannot coerce type 'closure' to vector of type
plain: You accidentally used a function where R expected data.
causes: Using a function name (like `mean`) instead of the result of the function (`mean(x)`).
Forgetting parentheses when calling a function.
fix: Look for places where you used a function name without calling it with parentheses.

plain: A function argument's default value refers to itself or creates a loop.
causes: Defining a function like `function(x = x)`.
An argument defaults to another argument that defaults back to the first.
fix: Fix the function definition so that default arguments use explicit values rather than referring to themselves.

plain: There is a circular dependency caused by lazy evaluation in R.
causes: Assigning a variable to itself within a function argument.
A variable name masks a function argument, causing an infinite loop when evaluated.
fix: Rename variables inside your function to avoid conflicting with the argument names.

plain: You are trying to call something as a function, but it is just a normal variable.
causes: Writing something like `5(x)` or `my_var(x)` where `my_var` is a number or data frame.
Missing an operator like `*` between a number and a parenthesis, e.g., `2(x+1)`.
fix: Check if you missed a multiplication sign or if you accidentally put parentheses right after a variable name.

plain: You are trying to subset data using the wrong number of dimensions (commas).
causes: Using `vec[1, 2]` on a 1-dimensional vector.
Using `df[1]` on a 2-dimensional data frame when you meant `df[1, ]`.
fix: If it's a vector, use one dimension `vec[index]`. If it's a data frame or matrix, use two dimensions `df[row, col]`.

plain: You are trying to extract a column that does not exist in the data frame.
causes: Typo in the column name.
The column was dropped or renamed in a previous step.
Using the wrong case (e.g., `Name` instead of `name`).
fix: Run `colnames(df)` to see the exact spelling and case of all available columns.

pattern: longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
plain: You are combining two vectors of different lengths, and R had to repeat the shorter one unevenly.
causes: Adding a vector of length 3 to a vector of length 5.
Comparing vectors of mismatched sizes.
fix: Make sure the vectors are the same length, or that the longer one is an exact multiple of the shorter one's length.

plain: R ran out of memory (RAM) trying to perform an operation or load data.
causes: Loading a dataset that is too large for your computer's memory.
Creating an extremely large matrix or performing a very memory-intensive calculation.
fix: Try removing unused objects with `rm()`, taking a sample of the data, or running the code on a machine with more RAM.

plain: You are using a function on a type of object it wasn't designed to handle.
causes: Calling a modeling function on plain text.
Passing a list into a function that requires a matrix.
fix: Check the class of your object using `class()`, and read the function's help page to see what types of objects it accepts.

plain: You are trying to create a data frame with duplicate row names.
causes: Setting `row.names` to a vector that contains repeating values.
Merging datasets in a way that duplicates row names.
fix: Ensure all row names are unique, or just let R generate automatic sequential row names.

plain: A mathematical function or plot received invalid numbers like Infinity or NaN (Not a Number).
causes: Dividing by zero, which creates `Inf`.
Passing limits to a plot (like `xlim` or `ylim`) that evaluate to `NA` or `Inf`.
fix: Check your data for `Inf`, `-Inf`, or `NaN` values and handle them before plotting or calculating.

plain: You tried to assign a value to a factor variable, but the value isn't an allowed category.
causes: Assigning "Apple" to a column that only allows "Banana" and "Orange".
A typo in the category name you are assigning.
fix: Check the allowed categories using `levels()`. If you need to add a new one, convert the factor to a character vector first.
